positions.name: CalibrationAuthorityByReference
positions.frame: how is calibration authority established when the claim is anchored to a named reference standard rather than to rank or role?
positions.why: Both expressions assert that the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration at 88.4 MHz was verified against the June reference plates. src-1 carries Quill's reported speech claiming full-band validity; src-4 compresses the same verification into a decision bullet. The shared directional read is the anchoring of authority to an external reference standard — the plates validate the claim, not the speaker's position.

positions.name: DecisionRatificationByFormatting
positions.frame: how does document formatting perform the settling of outcomes as ratified decisions?
positions.why: src-2 labels what follows as 'Key decisions,' performing ratification through the header itself. src-3 and src-4 adopt bolded label-and-value formatting under that header, enacting settled instrument and calibration choices through their structural placement rather than through argument or deliberation. The shared read is formatting as a ratification act.
